thread:
anika: sec-alert — alert-bot flagged a public gist that contains a token matching our ingest key pattern. gist: https://gist.github.com/anon/abcd1234

alert-bot: automated secret-scan: matched pattern `ri_live_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,}` in https://gist.github.com/anon/abcd1234 (confidence: 0.92)

mike: which env is that key for? prod/staging?

anika: looks like an ingest key. Quick vault lookup: key id `k_9f3b1` -> metadata: {env: prod, role: ingest, owner: acme-corp-project}.

sarah: ack. Revoke first, rotate, then check access logs. I'll start key invalidation now.

anika: steps: 1) revoke key 2) issue replacement and push to KMS 3) rotate client-side creds / redeploy 4) notify affected customers.

mike: running audit query now: `SELECT timestamp, src_ip, path FROM api_access WHERE api_key_id='k_9f3b1' AND timestamp > now()-interval '24 hours'`

mike: result: ~122 calls in last 6h from 3 distinct IPs; majority from 35.214.56.12 (suspicious hosting provider). No large data exfil counts, mostly small ingest pings.

sarah: I revoked `k_9f3b1` at 1718501300 (command: `rwctl keys revoke --id k_9f3b1 --force`). Confirmed revoke succeeded; outgoing traffic using that key is now 401.

anika: generating replacement key and storing in KMS. Using `rwctl keys create --owner acme-corp-project --role ingest --store-kms`. New key id `k_2a7d9`.

omplete: oliver: do we need to notify Acme? They own the project.

anika: yes — they have production integrations. We'll send an incident notice and remediation steps. Draft below.

oliver: draft email: "Hi Acme team — we detected a leaked ingest token associated with your project. We have revoked the affected token and issued a replacement. Please rotate your local configuration and restart ingestion clients. If you need assistance, reply and we'll help migrate keys."

sarah: also blocked offending IPs at perimeter WAF: added rule to drop 35.214.56.12 and related ASN ranges.

mike: opened ticket INC-2024-0987, attached audit logs and query results. I've set a follow-up job to monitor any retries or errors for the next 48h.

anika: post-incident actions (quick list):
- enable stricter GH secret scanning for all orgs + require zero-tolerance block on matches
- add pre-commit hook to detect `ri_` token patterns 
- enforce key creation RBAC: only owners + sec team can create prod ingest keys
- integrate KMS rotation policy (30d) for ephemeral tokens where possible
- increase audit-log retention for key events to 90 days
- write an RCA and publish internal postmortem

sarah: opened tasks in Tracker: TRK-4213 (GH scanning), TRK-4214 (RBAC policy), TRK-4215 (kms rotation). Assigned to devsec and infra owners.

mike: quick note: found one internal service that had the old key cached in a pod secret; rolled that pod and updated to new key. No customer data observed leaving cluster.

anika: action owners: Sarah -> key revocation + RBAC rule, Mike -> audit + monitoring, Oliver -> customer comms + support playbook, Anika -> KMS integration + postmortem.

oliver: customer notifications sent to Acme and BrightCo. Both acknowledged and are rotating on their side. BrightCo had only test traffic.

sarah: I'm going to run a full permissions audit on who can list/create keys (IAM check). Will follow up in this thread with findings.

anika: closing operational containment. We'll keep thread open for RCA edits and tracking. Please add any missed items. :thumbsup:

secbot: incident summary event created: INC-2024-0987, severity: medium, status: contained.

mike: final note: changed alert thresholds to raise priority for public gist matches and added a webhook to create tickets automatically.

anika: thanks team — excellent triage. Next steps: publish RCA by EOD tomorrow and review write-only KMS workflows for ingestion keys.
